title: Coherator adjunction and detection by global sections
statement: For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme Y, let D_QCoh(\mathcal O_Y) be the quasi-coherent full subcategory of D(\mathcal O_Y) [def-pc-derived-category]. The inclusion D_QCoh(\mathcal O_Y)\hookrightarrow D(\mathcal O_Y) has a right adjoint DQ_Y, so for M\in D_QCoh(\mathcal O_Y) and E\in D(\mathcal O_Y) there is a natural bijection Hom_{D(\mathcal O_Y)}(M,E)\cong Hom_{D_QCoh(\mathcal O_Y)}(M,DQ_Y E). Consequently, if u:E\to E' induces an isomorphism DQ_Y(u), then R\Gamma(Y,u):R\Gamma(Y,E)\to R\Gamma(Y,E') is a quasi-isomorphism; indeed H^i(Y,E)=Hom_{D(\mathcal O_Y)}(\mathcal O_Y[-i],E) and \mathcal O_Y[-i] is quasi-coherent.

proof.text: For qcqs Y, [lem-pc-derived-qcoh-compact-generation] says that D_QCoh(O_Y), with the shifts and distinguished triangles of D(O_Y), is compactly generated, and [lem-pc-derived-qcoh-direct-sums] says that it has all set-indexed coproducts. Its inclusion j into D(O_Y) is exact because the shifts and distinguished triangles of this full subcategory are those of the ambient derived category. The ambient category D(O_Y) has set-indexed coproducts by [lem-pc-derived-ambient-direct-sums]. The functor j preserves coproducts: for a family (E_i)_{i\in I} in D_QCoh(O_Y), the ambient sum E has H^q(E)\cong\bigoplus_i H^q(E_i) for every q by [lem-pc-derived-ambient-direct-sums]. This sheaf is the colimit, over the directed set of finite subsets J of I, of the finite sums \bigoplus_{i\in J}H^q(E_i). These finite sums are quasi-coherent by induction on |J| using [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-direct-sum], the empty sum 0 being quasi-coherent. Hence the colimit is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-colimit-affine-sections], so E lies in D_QCoh(O_Y) [def-pc-derived-category]. Because the subcategory is full, the ambient bijection Hom(E,G)\cong\prod_i Hom(E_i,G) for G in D_QCoh(O_Y) makes E a coproduct there. Thus every coproduct in D_QCoh(O_Y) is isomorphic to E, and j sends it to an ambient coproduct. Apply [lem-pc-brown-representability-right-adjoint] to j to obtain a right adjoint DQ_Y and its natural Hom bijection. The only scheme hypothesis needed here is qcqs, used by compact generation.

proof.text: Let u:E\to E' have DQ_Y(u) an isomorphism. Choose a K-injective complex I representing E. By [def-pc-global-derived-rhom], R\Gamma(Y,E) is represented by the complex of global sections of I, so its degree-i cohomology is the group of chain maps O_Y[-i] to I modulo homotopy (a map is an i-cocycle of global sections and a null homotopy is an i-coboundary). By [lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison], this group is Hom_{D(O_Y)}(O_Y[-i],E), naturally in E; the same holds for E'. The shift O_Y[-i] has only the quasi-coherent cohomology sheaf O_Y, hence belongs to D_QCoh(O_Y) by [def-pc-derived-category]. The adjunction of Step 1 identifies both Hom groups with Hom_{D_QCoh(O_Y)}(O_Y[-i],DQ_Y(-)), and DQ_Y(u) makes the induced map bijective. Thus every cohomology map of R\Gamma(Y,u) is an isomorphism, which is precisely a quasi-isomorphism.
